title: Word Transformation Chain
prompt:
Implement `transform_words(start, target, words, part)` for transformation chains between same-length words. A chain starts with `start`, ends with `target`, and every intermediate word must come from `words`. Duplicate words have no effect; `start` need not be in `words`; `target` is always a permitted final destination even when it is absent from `words`. Ignore dictionary words with a different length.

- `part == 1`: a move must change exactly one character; return whether a chain exists.
- `part == 2`: a move may change exactly one or exactly two characters; return whether a chain exists.
- `part == 3`: use the same move rule as part 2 and return one minimum-length chain including both endpoints, or `[]` when none exists.

If `start` and `target` have different lengths, return `False` for parts 1 and 2 and `[]` for part 3. If they are equal, return `True` for parts 1 and 2 and `[start]` for part 3. Raise `ValueError` for any other part. Use breadth-first search over the implicit graph; do not revisit a word.

example.reasoning: Changing one character at a time gives cold → cord → card → ward → warm. The target may be the final word even though it is absent from the dictionary.
